name: Gadajdu
body:
Gadajdu
CR 1

XP 400
CE Medium humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 11, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 16 (3d8+3)
Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +2; Weaknesses light sensitivity

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee bite +4 (1d3+2), slam +4 (1d4+2 plus grab)
Special Attacks clinging bite

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 13, Con 12, Int 8, Wis 13, Cha 8
Base Atk +2; CMB +4 (+8 grapple); CMD 15
Feats Great Fortitude, Skill Focus (Stealth)
Skills Climb +14, Perception +5, Stealth +8
Languages Gadajdu
SQ compression, expert climber

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Clinging Bite (Ex)

A gadajdu has a +2 circumstance bonus on attack rolls with its bite against a target it is grappling.

Expert Climber (Ex)

A gadajdu can climb virtually any surface, no matter how slick or sheer. In effect, the gadajdu is treated as constantly under a natural version of the spell spider climb with a climb speed of 30 feet.

Gadajdu are predatory humanoids that hunt in the dark network of tunnels which connect the daylit underworlds.

It waits, and like a spider, pounces on any animal or human victim that passes by. They speak their own strange chittering language and creep along walls, floors, ceilings, and small crevices with equal alacrity, able to move through seemingly impossibly small spaces without breaking stride. Some call them spiderfolk, but they have no particular affinity for arachnids, simply emulating their hunting tactics. Gadajdus do not like bright sunlight and are entirely nocturnal, fleeing with the first rays of dawn. Torchlight may give them pause but not for long, as hunger can drive them to leave the shadows and strike, hoping to disable their prey and drag it off into the darkness to feast upon at their leisure.
